cues.text: Hi everyone, I'm Maja Drabczyk and I'm head of policy and advocacy at Centrum Cyfrowe
a Think and Do Tank, based in Warsaw, focusing on openness and engagement in the digital realm.
The benefits of Open GLAM... Okay, that's a big one, but for me I think the starting
point is that I very very much believe in the public mission of cultural heritage institutions,
I believe that their operational actions, that division, should be based or built around the
needs of the society and I think that these days especially these days, I said I'm based in warsaw
and in my part of the world when we are in the middle of the of the crisis with the war
hitting on us from all corners, I think the need, the responsibility of
cultural heritage institutions to be there to act, to empower society is of high importance, is
of relevance, and how to best do it otherwise than by opening up yourself, your organization
otherwise than becoming inclusive otherwise than becoming an ethical entity supporting empowering
the society, your local communities, but also the bigger circle, and this is the value, this is the
biggest benefit, but also the responsibility of of CHIs of our sector. Again, making sure that
that we use the past, the collections that we have to support the contemporary, to support
different stakeholders, to educate to also entertain, but also i think to shape mindsets and
for this you need to open up you need to open up for dialogue you need to open up to also support
the development of technology to use data that we in the heritage sector have to help the technology
grow and improve in an ethical sense to fight disinformation to support growth of the society.
What are the biggest challenges barriers I think the first thing to say is of course copyright
but I want to focus on something else and I want to talk about the mindset of cultural
heritage professionals I think that still very often, and I don't mean it in the wrong way
but we see ourselves as custodians as protectors of the collections and this this attitude this
I think this a bit of scared that that they might be misused, I think holds us back from
engaging in in new collaborations in seeing and recognizing new opportunities
and allowing us it's stopping us from growing. So I would say that we need to overcome this or
maybe better to say we need to add new skills in our sector and see ourselves as facilitators as
experts or simply professionals willing to be engaged in a series of dialogues
being willing to be engaged in conversations being genuinely interested in the needs of our
stakeholders and making sure that through our actions we really respond to their needs and
we help them grow we help them shape mindsets we help them educate, and we help them entertain.
What inspired me recently was a conversation I took part in an online
chat we organized at tantrum to celebrate the Public Domain Day and we invited
to the online panel, a group of Polish experts and engaged together with us with Centrum
in a digitization project aimed at opening up of
collections of Polish national modern art gallery Zachęta and there were two
two statements that really stayed with me one coming from Olga Wysocka head of
she's Deputy Director at Zachęta, saying that you know everything that is
being funded through public money should be made available to the public and I think this
is the strong recognition of the of the public mission of of the institution that is
something that I and so clearly said and expressed this is something that I very much support
and I'm very much appreciative of. And next to that there was a uh there was a head of, CEO
of the big tech company supporting our actions in this project the digitization
and creation of online repository for Zachęta, Piotr Zientara, Xfaang
and he made this lovely comparison that I, that stayed with me too, saying that you know
IT projects, they're are more like cities and not houses, we are not building houses, and then just
renovate them, but we just constantly change evolve and this is like an endless process with a with
the biggest aim to remain useful, and I see exactly the work of the the cultural heritage sector
like that, that this is a continuous endless exercise that needs to be adjusted that
needs to be revised, that our strategies needs to be need to be adjusted and tailored to the
to the expectations of our users and this is where the the opening up of collections becomes of key
because how otherwise again we can remain relevant we can remain in dialogue with other sectors
and when it comes to the digital realm this is this is key again.
And how to begin how to start your path towards openness
just take baby steps, start small, start with a small collaboration with people coming from
outside of your usual bubble take a risk try something new invite others people with
different set of skills and expertise to help you understand the potential of your collections
when you decide to make a step and open up team up with educators team up with researchers
team up with creators team up with tech and see how much good you can
create together when being in dialogue when trying to understand the needs and your perspectives
they will be different and this is amazing so take the most of it enjoy the ride and just try.
